Engaging Forms —
Gamified Lead Generation
for eCommerce

A micro-SaaS product that lets small and medium eCommerce businesses run interactive quiz campaigns to capture leads — no developer needed, just a single script tag.

Overview

Turn passive visitors into qualified leads — through play

Engaging Forms is a lightweight SaaS tool built for small-to-medium eCommerce entrepreneurs who struggle to capture user data without expensive CRM integrations or developer resources. Merchants spin up gamified quiz campaigns on their website with a single copy-paste embed — and every quiz completion becomes a lead.

1
Script tag needed to activate the full platform on any website
∞
Campaigns a merchant can run under a single account
0
Lines of custom code required by the merchant’s team

The idea is deceptively simple: when a visitor takes a quiz on the merchant’s site, they must provide their email to receive their results. This mechanic turns engagement into a high-conversion lead pipeline — without pop-ups, generic forms, or friction.

The Problem

Small merchants are invisible to their own visitors

Most eCommerce lead generation tools are either too expensive, too complex to integrate, or produce low engagement. Smaller businesses face a specific set of compounding pain points:

Generic sign-up forms fail

Visitors scroll past newsletter pop-ups. There’s no perceived value in opting in to a brand they’ve just discovered.

Integration is a developer task

Most CRM tools require significant setup time and custom code — out of reach for solo operators and lean teams.

Design challenge: How do we create a lead generation experience so compelling that visitors actively want to provide their contact details — while keeping merchant setup under 5 minutes?

The Solution

Gamification as the trojan horse for lead capture

Engaging Forms flips the traditional lead generation dynamic. Instead of asking visitors to “subscribe” (transactional, low-value), it invites them to take a quiz (engaging, personally relevant). The email gate sits at the results stage — where motivation to complete is highest.

“Quiz results as the value exchange — visitors give their email to unlock a personalised outcome, not just to receive a newsletter.”

UI Design

UI Workflows — How It Works

View in Figma

Shown below are some of the major screens of the product, how it works.

01 Login & Signup

Split-panel auth design with geometric brand illustration on the right. Login supports forgot-password recovery flow; signup captures name, email, and password with T&C agreement before account creation.

02 Campaign Management

Empty state with onboarding illustration nudging merchants to create their first campaign.

Populated campaign list showing name, launch date, and live/inactive status toggle.

Campaign creation modal — just a name and domain. Simple by design.

Copy Script dialog presents the JS embed code immediately after creation — one paste into <head> activates the widget.

03 Notification Management

Empty notification state with CTA to create the first notification.

Notification list showing trigger delay, duration, and status toggle per item.

Campaign statistics: total views, mouse hovers, clicks, and submissions.

Create Notification modal — name the notification and choose between Quiz Contest or Emoji Feedback type before proceeding to the setup wizard.

04 Quiz Notification Setup Wizard

Step 1 — Welcome screen: set the quiz title, description, and CTA button text. Live preview renders the widget in real time.

Step 2 — Questions builder: add questions, options A/B, mark the correct answer, and add more questions dynamically.

Step 3 — Signup (email gate): configure the end-of-quiz capture screen where visitors submit their email to receive results.

05 Emoji Feedback Notification

The second notification type collects sentiment via emoji reactions (Angry, Sad, Neutral, Happy, Love). Merchants toggle which emotions to show and configure the title. The same Triggers, Display, and Customization settings used across all notification types.

06 End User — Live Widget on Website

The widget as seen by a visitor on the merchant’s site — a small, non-intrusive popup in the corner of the page. One click launches the quiz experience without navigating away from the merchant’s content.

Design Decisions

Key choices that shaped the product

1

Email gate at results, not at entry

Placing the email capture after quiz completion maximises intent. By the time a visitor has answered 3–5 questions, they’ve invested time and are curious about their result — motivation to hand over an email is at its peak. Entry gates showed significantly higher drop-off in early testing.

2

Campaign-per-domain model

Rather than one global embed code, a campaign-per-domain architecture lets merchants A/B test different quiz types across subdomains, track performance independently, and cleanly separate brands if they operate multiple storefronts.

3

Single script tag as the entire integration

The biggest friction point for the target audience is technical setup. Everything — widget rendering, campaign config, lead submission — is handled server-side. Merchants only paste one <script> tag into their site header.

4

Wizard-based builder with live preview

The stepped setup with a persistent live preview panel on the right reduces cognitive load. Merchants see exactly how their widget will appear on their site as they build it, eliminating guesswork and revision cycles.
